..
As of 255 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Heat and humidity persists today with isolated to 
scattered showers and storms possible late this afternoon into this 
evening.

Afternoon weather analysis showed generally zonal flow aloft with a 
shortwave moving from OH into WV noted by a change to NW flow aloft. 
At the surface, the Bermuda high continues to remain off the SE 
coast. As such, hot and humid conditions continue with temps as of 2 
PM in the lower 90s and heat indices around 100F. Afternoon highs in 
the low-mid 90s are expected with heat indices around 100F.

The latest radar indicates a healthy MCS across WV into far S PA. 
This line of storms is much more robust than CAMs showed. As such, 
it remains unclear how much this line of storms will hold together 
as it crosses the mountains of WV/VA. CAMs generally show only 
isolated convection east of the mountains later this afternoon into 
this evening apart from the ARW which keeps convection going all the 
way to the coast. While mesoanalysis shows some lingering MLCIN 
across SE VA/NE NC, it also shows S winds east of the mountains 
(presumably due to a lee trough) and 1500-2500 J/kg of MLCAPE. With 
S winds (as opposed to SW winds that CAMs had) and an unstable 
environment east of the mountains with favorable low-level 
instability along and north of I-64, it is entirely possible 
that CAMs are wrong and this line of storms continues into 
central VA later this afternoon into this evening. If it does, a
severe risk for predominantly damaging winds will exist. 
Currently SPC has a marginal risk (level 1/5) for severe storms 
along and north of I-64 with a portion of Dorchester County in a
slight risk (level 2/5). However, if the storms do make it 
across the mountains, this threat may need to be expanded and/or
increased. Outside of the severe potential, locally heavy 
rainfall is possible with any storms. WPC has a marginal ERO 
across far northern portions of the area to account for this 
potential. Convection should taper off overnight with remnant 
cloud cover potentially lingering. Lows tonight in the 70s are 
expected.


KEY MESSAGE 2...An unsettled pattern continues through the remainder 
of the week. However, uncertainty remains high.

NW/WNW flow aloft develops Tue through the remainder of the week as 
a ridge aloft builds across the central CONUS while a trough lingers 
across New England and Canada. At the surface, the Bermuda high will 
start to break down. This will allow for an active pattern to 
persist with a daily potential for isolated to scattered storms each 
afternoon/evening. CAMs show multiple rounds of MCSs developing in 
the WNW/NW flow aloft. However, where they track and when they 
develop will have large implications to the local weather. Most CAMs 
have an overturned airmass moving into the region in the wake of 
today's MCS for Tue. As such, HREF (as well as most individual 
models/CAMs) show dew points in the upper 60s to around 70F Tue 
afternoon (as opposed to the mid 70s from the NBM) and lower 
surface temps. Therefore, have blended in lower guidance for dew
points but held off (for now) on dropping high temps by more 
than a degree or two due to uncertainty regarding whether or not
partial clearing can occur during the afternoon. This resulted 
in heat indices remaining below heat advisory criteria. As such,
no heat headlines will be issued at this time. Will note that 
latest guidance keeps temps even cooler than the current 
forecast. In general, highs in lower 90s are the most likely 
scenario with locally upper 80s or mid 90s possible Tue. 
Additionally, as a result of the overturned airmass, widespread 
cloud cover and mixed dew points could result in very little 
instability Tue afternoon. HREF mean CAPE only shows around 500 
J/kg for most of the area (which for August is very low). As 
such, confidence in storm development (and especially severe 
potential) for Tue has decreased substantially. Nevertheless, 
SPC has maintained a marginal risk (1/5) for severe storms 
across most of the area with a slight risk (level 2/5) across 
portions of Piedmont. WPC has also maintained a marginal ERO 
across the area for Tue.

SPC has maintained a marginal risk (level 1/5) for severe storms 
across southern portions of the FA Wed. However, confidence 
continues to remain low given uncertainty in aforementioned MCS
timing and impacts. For now, have largely kept NBM PoPs 
(15-35%) to account for the potential for isolated to scattered 
storms. By Tue, models should have a better handle on what 
weather we can expect for Wed. Beyond Wed, the pattern remains 
similar with only a slight chance (15-20%) for a few isolated 
showers or storms on Thu with a better chance on Fri (30-50% 
PoPs). Outside of convection, temps remain near normal with 
highs in the upper 80s to lower 90s Wed and Thu and mid 80s to 
lower 90s Fri.
